en.title: MAR 1.1.2(1)(b): is an offer that meets both (2)(c) and (2)(d) meant to lose the placement exemption?
en.summary: MAR 1.1.2(1)(b) exempts an offer by way of placement only if it satisfies "one and one only" of the conditions in (2); (1)(c) allows combinations only where one of them is (a), (b) or (m). An offer of Securities denominated in units of at least USD 100,000 (condition (d)) and issued at or above that amount also meets condition (c), because every investor pays at least USD 100,000. Read literally, such an offer is not exempt unless it also meets (a), (b) or (m), while the same offer issued below USD 100,000 per unit would be. For Exempt Securities, MAR 1.2.2(1) uses "one or more of the conditions". The words "one and one only" may be meant to stop the stacking of exemptions, but the text does not say which combinations are excluded.
en.correction: Please confirm whether an offer that meets both conditions 1.1.2(2)(c) and (d) is meant to lose the exemption unless 1.1.2(1)(c) applies. If not, please consider "one or more of the conditions", or name the conditions that may not be combined.
